title: Coconut lemon curd
summary: A sharp, spoonable lemon curd of coconut cream softly set with a little agar and blended smooth, sweetened with allulose so it stays silky in the fridge; vegan as written.
steps: In a small saucepan (not aluminium, which reacts with the acid), whisk the agar into the cold coconut cream until no specks remain. Whisk in the allulose, salt, turmeric and zest.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, whisking, and boil 2 minutes so the agar fully dissolves.
Off the heat, whisk in the coconut oil, then the lemon juice. Adding the juice after the boil keeps the acid from weakening the agar.
Pour into a shallow container and refrigerate about 1 hour, until set to a soft, sliceable gel.
Scrape the gel into a blender or use a stick blender and blend 30–60 seconds until it turns smooth, glossy and spoonable, like a classic curd. Press through a sieve if you want it without zest.
Spoon into a jar, press plastic wrap onto the surface and refrigerate. Keeps about 1 week.
tips: Setting and then blending is what gives agar a curd's soft, creamy body; stirred while it sets, it turns lumpy instead.
For a spreadable curd with no set at all, skip the agar and blend 0.25 tsp xanthan gum into the cooled mixture; it stays a little looser and never firms up.
Unlike an egg curd it cannot curdle, but it tastes of coconut as well as lemon; refined coconut cream brands vary, so pick a mild one.

origin.history: Lemon curd, once also called 'lemon cheese', became a popular English spread for bread, scones and tarts in the 1800s, made with lemon juice, sugar, eggs and butter. Egg-free curds thickened with cornflour or custard powder have long existed as economical versions. The coconut-based vegan curd set with agar or gums is a more recent development of plant-based cooking, and has no single known originator.
